content.intro: Learn csrf protection in forms through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: CSRF Protection in Forms matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines csrf protection in forms as part of forms and user input. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Cross-site request forgery; CSRF tokens; Middleware requirements; Safe handling of form submissions; Testing CSRF behavior. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Cross-site request forgery
items.text: Cross-site request forgery is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: CSRF tokens
items.text: CSRF protection verifies that a state-changing browser request is associated with a valid token. Keep middleware/template token use and safe-cookie/HTTPS configuration aligned; CSRF is not an authorization substitute.

items.title: Middleware requirements
items.text: Middleware hooks into request/response processing. Keep it focused, order it correctly, and ensure it returns a response when it short-circuits the request.

items.title: Safe handling of form submissions
items.text: Safe handling of form submissions is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Testing CSRF behavior
items.text: A good test covers an observable contract and asserts status, output, database changes or access denial. Include invalid and boundary inputs so a regression does not only fail on a happy path.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: CSRF Protection in Forms
content_blocks.code:
form = ContactForm(request.POST)
if form.is_valid():
    cleaned = form.cleaned_data
    # Use validated fields; send/persist through application logic.
else:
    # Re-render the bound form and its field errors.
    pass
content_blocks.expected_output: valid submissions expose normalized values through cleaned_data; invalid submissions keep field errors that templates can present.
